has been observed pinned at the repo's very first commit. A plain `git checkout -b <name> main`
  silently branches from that frozen history and the next script that expects current content
  (e.g. a `.claudinite/` path) fails confusingly. Always `git fetch origin main` and branch from
  `origin/main` explicitly (#73).

- **Reaching step 6 of a work-item run** (`node .../scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs`) — it will
  fail here: the script's read/write path (`signals/gh.mjs`) is documented in its own header as
  Action-side only ("everything session-side stays MCP-only"), and this session's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is
  a proxy placeholder the REST API rejects outright ("GitHub access is not enabled for this
  session"), confirmed across attempts with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` set, with `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`,
  and via raw `curl`. Don't re-diagnose it — go straight to replicating the transition by hand
  over the GitHub MCP tools: the execution-record comment in `run-record.mjs`'s exact format
  (`claudinite-task-exec v1 <pack>/<task> [#<n>] <status>`), the `task:agent`→outcome label swap,
  the close with the matching `state_reason`, and (what `readyDependents` would have released) a
  check for any open item naming `Blocked-by: #<n>`. Four independent sessions in one day each lost
  2–5 minutes rediscovering this same dead end (#126, #130, #133, #166); a fifth still ran the
  script itself twice — once without `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` set, once with — before switching to the
  manual path, costing ~77s despite this very rule already being loaded in context (#202): don't
  just skip re-diagnosing a failure, skip attempting the script at all. And the manual replication
  above is written for the `done` outcome only — on `approval`, the real script's
  `OUTCOMES.approval.record` is `null` (post no `claudinite-task-exec` line), the item stays
  **open** rather than closing, and the labels are `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-approval`
  rather than an outcome-label swap; post that shape directly rather than posting the `done` shape
  and then a correction comment (#212).

- **Comparing against `origin/main` in a fresh checkout** — an explicit `git fetch origin main` is
  not always enough by itself: this container's checkout can be shallow, and fetching a named
  branch does not force-update an already-existing stale remote-tracking ref. `origin/main` showed
  frozen at the initial commit even right after fetching it by name, producing a bogus wall-to-wall
  diff. Check `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` first, and `git fetch origin main --unshallow`
  before trusting any `git diff`/`git log` against `origin/main` (#197).

- **Looking up a PR by its head branch** — `mcp__github__list_pull_requests` with a bare branch name
  in `head` (no `owner:` prefix) does not filter; it can silently hand back an unrelated PR as if it
  matched, for every branch queried, with no error to flag the miss. Qualify `head` as
  `owner:branch-name`, or skip the lookup and go straight to the git-based `merge-base`/
  `diff --stat` check the `single-branch-status` skill already uses as its fallback (#213).

- **Writing a PR or issue body that cross-references an object you're about to create** — don't
  guess its number. Issue/PR numbers share one counter per repo, and the object you're creating
  consumes one too; a PR body written before its companion issue exists can end up citing the wrong
  number once the issue actually lands. Create the referenced object first, or leave a placeholder
  and patch the body once the number is known (#24).

- **Waiting on background subagents or tasks with nothing left to do between notifications** —
  don't manufacture a no-op Bash call (`sleep 1; echo waiting`, `true`) just to occupy a turn; say
  so in plain text with no tool call instead. A bare no-op tool call can come back with no visible
  text at all, which the harness then has to interrupt to ask for a real response — pure waste next
  to just writing the status line (#214).

Closes #201 — `claudinite-growth/growth-extract`.

## Activity half — nothing new

Read all 6 substantive commits, PR #229, and all 10 issues in the window's Context. All of it was
Claudinite's own bookkeeping: automated engine/pack self-update merges (#224/#198), mechanical
"deliver withheld workflow files from staging" steps, ten templated `fleet-adoption`/`fleet-drift`
issues with no discussion, and PR #229 — itself an in-flight, unmerged rule-revalidation correction
to this repo's own `RULES.md`. Nothing here clears the bar for a new lesson.

## Conversation half — 14 logs mined

Read both required windows off `origin/conversation-logs`: the last 24h (issue-197, 213, 210, 202,
214, 211, 212, 209) and the branch's oldest 24h (issue-2, 22, 24, 28, 30, 32). Landed the friction
signals that were genuinely new and durable, after dedupe against the existing pack (a few
candidates — a `Comment class:` miss, a self-polling PR reminder now covered by the owner's own
personal preference, an environment-plumbing Chromium-path guess, an already-stale
`.claudinite-checks.json` fact superseded by this window's own rename — did **not** clear the bar
and are not included):

- Widened the tracker-hunt bullet: `list_issues`'s `query` param shares `search_issues`'s
  unreliability, and `minimal_output: true` alone doesn't bound an overflow (#209, #210).
- Widened the `converge-item.mjs` bullet: a fifth session still ran the script itself before
  switching to the manual path (#202), and the manual replication needed the `approval`-outcome
  shape spelled out separately from `done` (#212).
- New: shallow-clone checkouts can show a stale `origin/main` even right after an explicit fetch
  by name — `--unshallow` is required (#197).
- New: `list_pull_requests`'s `head` filter needs an `owner:` qualifier or it silently mismatches
  (#213).
- New: never guess an unborn issue/PR's number inside a body being published (#24).
- New: don't manufacture a no-op Bash call while waiting on background tasks (#214).
- New: an overflowed `search_issues`/`search_code` result always parses as GitHub's
  `{total_count, incomplete_results, items}` envelope (#212).

## Upgrade pass

All landed lessons are about agent/tool runtime behavior, not a static signature in the repo's own
files — none clear the check-the-world test, so all stayed prose.

`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 0 advisory.

{"number":24,"title":"Retire references to the Sheepdog repo across the fleet, replacing them with Shepherd","body":"## Problem

`missingbulb/Shepherd` is now the fleet enforcer, but `missingbulb/Sheepdog` — a **separate repo**, not a rename — is still named by references across the fleet. The most consequential are the `claude-code-web-users-support` store declarations: **11 repos** point their preferences store at the old repo, so a web session in any of them reads preferences from a repo that is being retired.

The `fleet-pack-seeds` sweep cannot fix this: it seeds and never overrides, so a member that already carries a config keeps its stale value forever. This needs a direct sweep.

This is about the **repo**, not the `sheepdog` **pack** — the pack keeps its name, and every mention of the pack, `parseSheepdogConfig`, the pack directory, and `sheepdog/fleet-*` task ids stays exactly as it is.

## Scope

**Live references — rewrite:**
- [ ] Member `.claudinite-checks.json` store declarations (11 repos)
- [ ] Canon's own declaration and the `claude-code-web-users-support` migration record's `declarePacks`
- [ ] `claudinite-dashboard` example `redirectUri` and roster comment
- [ ] Test fixtures naming the enforcer repo (including the `hashedMinute` golden)
- [ ] Canon local-pack prose that directs a session at the enforcer

**Deliberately left alone:**
- `Sheepdog#172` issue citations — the issue genuinely lives in the old repo
- `docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md` Phase 3 repo list — a dated rollout record, and this repo carries a standing `reference-integrity` accept declaring that doc's names deliberate history

## Fleet config

- [ ] Add `missingbulb/Sheepdog` to `exclude` in this repo's sheepdog pack config, so the sweeps stop covering the retired enforcer
- [ ] Archive the old repo (owner-only step — tracked separately)

## Blocked

- `missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite` — this session's GitHub credential has no access to it. It carries both a stale store declaration and a `Sheepdog` mention in `product-wiki/Positioning/README.md`.

1	// The machine-readable records a task's execution leaves in an Actions log
2	// (skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §4.2), and the parsers that read them back.
3	//
4	// TWO FAMILIES, ONE OF THEM HISTORICAL. `claudinite-task-run` was the SLOT
5	// scheduler's own line, one per due task per run; the slot scheduler is retired
6	// (#974) and nothing writes that line any more. The parser stays, and only the
7	// parser: Actions logs from before the retirement are still inside their retention
8	// window, and the usage fold still counts them. Nothing new should be taught this
9	// shape — `claudinite-task-exec` below is the live record.
10	//
11	// The counts these produce are exact within the Actions log retention window, and
12	// that is worth stating next to the capture-derived counts they land beside.
13	
14	// The five things a slot scheduler run could do with a due task. One name per
15	// outcome, used verbatim as the counter key in the aggregate, so there is no
16	// mapping table between "what the run said" and "what the fold counted" to drift.
17	export const TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze([
18	  // A dispatch issue was filed: an agent session ran this task.
19	  'agent',
20	  // The task ran with NO agent — an `agent_model: none` task (code-work is the
21	  // whole task), or an agentful one whose code-work requested no agent phase.
22	  // Kebab, not the declaration field's `code_work`: this word is a WIRE token,
23	  // constrained to the line format's `[a-z-]+` charset.
24	  'code-work',
25	  // Due, but its precondition said there was nothing to do.
26	  'skipped',
27	  // Its code-work failed; the run converged the task to a needs-human issue.
28	  'failed',
29	  // Due and past its precondition, but no NEW agent run started: this slot was
30	  // already dispatched (exactly-once), an earlier dispatch is still open
31	  // (at-most-one-open), or another task claimed the run exclusively. Work that
32	  // was wanted and did not happen this run.
33	  'deferred',
34	]);
35	
36	// An empty per-task counter row — every outcome present, zeros included, so a row's
37	// shape never depends on which outcomes a task happened to hit.
38	export const emptyTaskRun = () => Object.fromEntries(TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.map((o) => [o, 0]));
39	
40	// The line format. `v1` is the shape's version: a reader that meets a `v2` line
41	// knows it is looking at something it was not written for, instead of silently
42	// half-parsing it.
43	export const TASK_RUN_TAG = 'claudinite-task-run';
44	const VERSION = 'v1';
45	
46	// Actions stamps every log line with its own timestamp before the command's output,
47	// so the parse tolerates that prefix — without it, a fetched log reads as having
48	// printed nothing at all.
49	const LINE_RE = new RegExp(
50	  String.raw`^(?:\S+\s+)?${TASK_RUN_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
51	);
52	
53	// One line → `{ pack, task, slotId, outcome }`, or null for anything that is not a
54	// record of this version. Deliberately strict: an unknown outcome word is NOT a
55	// record, because counting it would mint a counter key nothing ever reads.
56	// The code phase has been renamed twice, and job logs outlive both renames:
57	// `preprocess` (pre-2026-08-06) and `prework` (pre-2026-08-18) are the earlier
58	// words for what is now `code-work`. Runs logged under either still parse, each
59	// normalized straight to the canonical word.
60	// Exported because the outcome words are also the usage aggregate's counter KEYS,
61	// and that file holds rows written under the older words. Its decode renames them
62	// by this same map, so a rename never silently drops a historical count.
63	export const LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze({ preprocess: 'code-work', prework: 'code-work' });
64	
65	export function parseTaskRun(line) {
66	  const m = LINE_RE.exec(line);
67	  if (!m) return null;
68	  const [, pack, task, slotId, word] = m;
69	  const outcome = LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES[word] ?? word;
70	  if (!TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.includes(outcome)) return null;
71	  return { pack, task, slotId, outcome };
72	}
73	
74	// Every record in one job log. The log is the whole job's output — this picks its
75	// own lines out of it and ignores everything else.
76	export function parseTaskRuns(text) {
77	  const out = [];
78	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
79	    const rec = parseTaskRun(line);
80	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
81	  }
82	  return out;
83	}
84	
85	// --- executor-side execution records ------------------------------------------
86	// The historical records above say what the retired slot scheduler DID with a due
87	// task; these record what an EXECUTOR SESSION did with the work it ran. Printed by executor-side code
88	// (resolve-dispatch on a terminal verdict, record-exec.mjs at convergence), they
89	// land in the session transcript, ride to the conversation-logs branch with the
90	// executor's capture step, and the usage fold counts them deterministically —
91	// the "task statuses out of the conversation logs" half of the census (owner,
92	// 2026-08-06). Same single-home rule: renderer and parser sit here together.
93	
94	export const TASK_EXEC_STATUSES = Object.freeze([
95	  // The dispatch ran to completion within its ceiling; the issue was closed.
96	  'success',
97	  // The run failed (task failure or ceiling violation); converged to needs-human.
98	  'failed',
99	  // The dispatch named a task the repo no longer carries (file gone, pack
100	  // undeclared) — the executor closed the issue as obsolete. Not a failure.
101	  'task-gone',
102	  // The dispatch was malformed (bad path shape, unparseable declaration) and was
103	  // converged to needs-human without running.
104	  'invalid',
105	]);
106	
107	export const TASK_EXEC_TAG = 'claudinite-task-exec';
108	
109	// The bracketed field is the OCCURRENCE'S IDENTITY, which is a different thing under
110	// each dispatch mechanism: a slot id (`d2026-08-06`) where slots decide what runs, and
111	// the work item's issue number (`#867`) where the queue does. `slotId` keeps its name
112	// for the fielded records that already carry one; what it must never become is a
113	// constant, since it is the only join from a record back to the work it describes.
114	export const renderTaskExec = ({ pack, task, slotId, status }) =>
115	  `${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} ${pack}/${task} [${slotId ?? 'unknown'}] ${status}`;
116	
117	const EXEC_LINE_RE = new RegExp(
118	  String.raw`(?:^|\s)${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
119	);
120	
121	export function parseTaskExec(line) {
122	  const m = EXEC_LINE_RE.exec(line);
123	  if (!m) return null;
124	  const [, pack, task, slotId, status] = m;
125	  if (!TASK_EXEC_STATUSES.includes(status)) return null;
126	  return { pack, task, slotId, status };
127	}
128	
129	export function parseTaskExecs(text) {
130	  const out = [];
131	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
132	    const rec = parseTaskExec(line);
133	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
134	  }
135	  return out;
136	}
